items.headline: Converse made a fluffy running-shoe slipper
items.caption: The T-Bone Slide Moccasin Boa mixes UGG vibes with a chunky foam sole.
body: It's from Converse Japan, known for quirky remixes.
Fur collar on top, runner's sole below.
How to wear it: around the house, or with sweatpants out.

items.headline: New Balance's 'Breakfast Tea' skate shoe
items.caption: Franky Villani's Numeric 417 comes in a warm tan.
body: It mixes suede, canvas and mesh.
The same colour also appeared on a Numeric 993.
How to wear it: with brown cords and a white tee.

items.headline: Vans puts worn-in corduroy on its Slip-on
items.caption: The Premium Classic Slip-on 98 gets scuffed, vintage-look cord.
body: It's a cosy update for colder weather.
Looks like a well-loved pair already.
How to wear it: with straight jeans and white socks.

items.headline: This season's best sweaters, draped on designer chairs
items.caption: Stylist Colin King shows off fall knits the way we all do.
body: He threw them over French modern chairs from Demisch Danant.
It's a smart way to see how a knit falls.
How to wear it: a chunky knit, loosely over a shirt.

items.headline: The 25-year-old behind an eight-figure streetwear brand
items.caption: Mertra founder Aron Williams on starting out and clothes that react.
body: Mertra makes jackets that change colour when touched.
It has worked with Umbro and artist Slawn.
Style lesson: one fun piece makes an outfit.

items.headline: 21 coats and jackets worth wanting this fall
items.caption: GQ's pick of the season's outerwear.
body: Fall lets you mix textures and colours freely.
Outerwear is the best part of it.
How to wear it: one good coat over everything.

items.headline: What to wear to a house party
items.caption: From warehouse parties to dinner parties, GQ has the fit.
body: It's the first of GQ's new 'The Invitation' column.
Different parties, different dress codes.
How to wear it: dark knit, good trousers, clean shoes.

items.headline: Pierce Brosnan's MobLand coats show who's boss
items.caption: Conrad Harrigan's coats signal power in season two.
body: Tom Hardy does the dirty work; Brosnan's coats sign it off.
Esquire picks how to get the look.
How to wear it: a long camel or charcoal overcoat.

items.headline: How to get every Tom Hardy haircut
items.caption: From the noughties sweep to his short back and sides.
body: Barbers explain each look, from Bane to Peaky Blinders.
His current cut is a neat short back and sides.
Style lesson: match your cut to your face, not a film.

items.headline: Ralph Lauren named menswear designer of the year
items.caption: Esquire Australia's roundup of November's menswear news.
body: Lauren was honoured at the American Museum of Natural History.
The monthly roundup also covers new drops and trends.
Style lesson: classic never goes out of style.

items.headline: How to spend $250 at a watch fair
items.caption: Two Hodinkee editors take on a budget challenge at Windup New York.
body: Windup is now in its eleventh edition.
It draws thousands of collectors every year.
Style lesson: a great watch doesn't need a big budget.

items.headline: A family dog spotted a baby's racing heartbeat
items.caption: Doberman Saraya wouldn't leave six-month-old Alexander's side.
body: Doctors found his heart beating at 280 beats a minute.
His mum says the dog likely saved his life.

items.headline: After walking 28 years, an adventurer hugs his mum
items.caption: Karl Bushby walked 31,000 miles to get home to Hull.
body: He set off from Chile in 1998.
He thanked the kindness of strangers around the world.

items.headline: Geothermal heat is cutting housing energy bills
items.caption: Vermont Gas launched the state's first community-scale geothermal project.
body: A US study found geothermal heat pumps cut a New York complex's energy costs by about 40%.
Utilities see it as a way to lower bills.
